PullRequest.Title: sessions: apply a consistent context menu structure in the Agents window
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:

  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.

-->

Several Agents window context menus had drifted from a consistent structure: Delete sat mid-menu, related actions were split across groups, and the same object offered different menus in different places. This applies one structure, following VS Code, Windows, and Apple menu guidelines, to all of them:

```
navigation   open, create, run
1_state      read/unread, done/restore, enable/disable
2_organize   pin, groups, move
3_copy       copy link, copy path, duplicate/export
4_manage     settings, rename, delete (destructive last)
```

## Changes

**Sessions list session row**
```
Open to the Side · New Nested Session · Import · Open Pull Request
───
Mark as Read/Unread · Mark Nested Sessions as Read · Mark as Done / Restore
───
Pin/Unpin · Add to Group / Move to Group › · Create Group · Remove from Group
───
Copy Link · Copy Pull Request URL
───
Settings › · Rename... · Delete...
```
- The group actions are merged into the Organize group after Pin instead of being appended after a final separator.
- The list-wide Mark All as Read that appeared on every session in Date grouping now lives on the Recent and Older section headers and only marks that section. The nested action is renamed **Mark Nested Sessions as Read**.

**Other menus**
- **Nested chat row:** Open Parent Session · Open to the Side | read state · Mark as Done/Restore | Move Up · Move Down · Promote to Session | Copy Link | Rename... · Delete...
- **Chat tab:** same structure, adding Close and Mark as Read/Unread; Delete Chat becomes Delete... (it confirms).
- **Session header and its overflow menu:** pane actions first (Close, Maximize, Session Layout ›, Side Chats ›, Show Chat Tabs ›), then read/done state, Pin, Copy Link, Rename... and Delete Chat. Un-maximize now reads **Restore Size** so it can't collide with Restore.
- **Section and group headers:** their inline toolbar actions (New Session, New Quick Chat, Mark All as Done, Configure External Sessions) now also appear in their context menus, through new `SessionSectionContext` and `SessionGroupContext` menus. Group headers offer Mark All as Read in Date grouping too, and comparison groups no longer offer the unrelated Create Group.
- **Automation card (More Actions):** Open on GitHub | Enable/Disable | Duplicate... · Export... | Delete...
- **Automation history row:** Open on GitHub · Stop | read state · Mark as Done/Restore | Rename...
- **AI customization file:** Open · Run Prompt | Enable/Disable | Copy Path | Delete...
- **Project bar:** Customize... (opens a quick pick).

**Extension and docs**
- **Copilot extension:** its Copilot CLI Rename contribution moves to `4_manage@2`. Third-party extensions using the old group IDs (such as `1_edit`) will need the same update.
- **Skill:** adds a `context-menus` skill describing the group order and rules, referenced from `best-practices.instructions.md`, so future menus follow the same structure.

## How to test

1. In the Agents window, right-click a session, a nested chat, a chat tab, the session header, a section header, a custom group header, an automation history row, and an AI customization file. Check the order above and that Delete is always last.
2. On an automation card, open More Actions and check the order.
3. Switch the Sessions list to Date grouping and check that Recent, Older, and custom group headers offer Mark All as Read.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`: passed
- `npm run eslint -- <changed TypeScript files>`: passed
- `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob "vs/sessions/**/*.test.js"`: 8670 passing, 24 pending

New tests snapshot the full session row menu, the nested chat menu order, the Date section header action, and the chat tab Close and read state commands.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a session row, nested-chat row, chat-tab, section-header, group-header, automation, customization, or session-header context menu
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A user right-click synchronously reads local observable/context-key state, constructs a small action list, sorts/joins menu groups, and paints the context menu. No subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network operation is on this menu-opening critical path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Session-row menus scale with selected sessions and configured custom groups; section headers additionally scan the section's sessions/workspace folders and configured groups; tab menus scale with visible chat tabs during a tab rebuild. These are local in-memory collections and context menus are user-triggered rather than render/frame loops.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single synchronous UI event; menu construction is serialized on the UI thread. Header and item menu instances are disposed on hide or replacement, and tab action instances are disposed whenever tabs rebuild.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Menus are intentionally rebuilt from current context state on each opening; there is no remote cache or cache miss. Static registrations are reused, while per-opening menu/listener resources have explicit disposal.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the synchronous call path and cleanup because the tree context-menu dispatcher, menu creation, action joining, and onHide disposal were traced directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very large session/group collections could increase local menu-opening CPU and allocation, but realistic menus contain a bounded number of actions and the only newly added scan occurs once per right-click; there is no evidence of measurable latency or a hot-loop regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff mostly reorders existing actions; new header menu construction is bounded to explicit user interaction, performs only local work, and cleans up its menu resources.

Scenarios.Scenario: Use Mark All as Read from a Date section or custom-group header
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After the user selects the action, the list filters the target sessions and awaits ISessionsManagementService.markAllRead. That method waits for all selected provider updates before the command completes; this work is not performed merely by opening the context menu.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Update read state through each session provider; Agent Host dispatches read-state changes to its connection, including per-unread-chat updates when independent chat read state is supported, while the Copilot provider update is local observable state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One top-level update per unread, non-archived, non-automation session in the chosen section/group; Agent Host may additionally dispatch once per unread aggregate chat. Date-section cardinality is now the chosen Recent/Older section rather than all sessions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: In Date grouping, a session-row action marked every unread session globally. Non-Date section/group headers already exposed the same provider path. The diff moves Date-mode access to narrower section/group headers, reducing or preserving effective cardinality rather than increasing it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The action awaits all provider updates, so the slowest update controls completion; menu opening itself does not wait on this boundary.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective cardinality is unread eligible sessions in the selected section/group after filtering, plus unread aggregate chats for Agent Host sessions. This is less than or equal to the old Date-mode global action for the same list state.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: markAllRead uses Promise.all across target sessions. Within an Agent Host session, unread chats are updated sequentially; independent sessions can update concurrently. No new limiter or additional concurrency is introduced by this PR.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Read state is current observable/provider state and is not cached or negatively cached. There is no coalescing, but the diff narrows the target set and does not add retries.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the action's filtering closure, markAllRead Promise.all implementation, and both provider implementations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider latency and the number of unread nested chats vary, but the before/after cardinality comparison is clear: the changed Date workflow cannot fan out to more sessions than the removed global action.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Although the command reaches provider/IPC boundaries with collection-scaled concurrency, the PR replaces a broader global Date action with section/group-scoped updates and therefore does not introduce or amplify the fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run New Session, Archive/Mark All as Done, or Configure External Sessions from the newly added section/group context menus
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Opening the menu performs no boundary work. Selecting New Session opens the existing composer/session flow; selecting Archive/Done runs the existing confirmation then serial archiveSessionsWithUndo path; configuring external sessions writes the existing user configuration value.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Archive each selected session through its provider; active requests may first acquire/load chat state and cancel the request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One serial archive operation per non-archived session in the section/group, plus cancellation/load work only for active chats.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The identical Action2 command and archive implementation were already exposed from the section/group inline toolbar; the diff adds another menu entry point without changing the operation, cardinality, ordering, or concurrency.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs only after explicit action selection and is awaited serially to preserve partial-batch undo semantics.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist the external-session visibility/grouping preference through IConfigurationService.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One configuration update when the user toggles a submenu item.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same submenu and configuration action already existed in the section toolbar/filter menu; this PR only exposes that submenu in the section context menu.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited only after choosing the setting; it is off the context-menu opening path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Archive cost scales with eligible sessions in the selected section/group and active chats per session. The context-menu route supplies the same section/group object as the pre-existing toolbar route.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Archive operations remain deliberately serial; configuration updates are single operations; session creation follows the existing single-command flow.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache is added or bypassed. Existing session/provider state and configuration services remain authoritative.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence because the new registrations point to unchanged Action2 run methods and the transitive archive/configuration implementations were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Archive duration depends on provider and active-chat state, but no changed code alters that duration or multiplicity.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. These are alternate entry points to existing commands; expensive work remains deferred until selection and has unchanged cardinality/concurrency.

Scenarios.Scenario: Use Close or Mark as Read/Unread from a chat-tab context menu
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A right-click locally chooses actions from current chat/session capabilities. Selecting Close or read state invokes the shared command service and awaits the existing single-chat/session management path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist one chat/session read-state change through the owning provider; Agent Host can dispatch the change over its connection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One selected chat/session per click; no per-tab loop invokes provider work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same shared read/close commands were available from list/header surfaces, but not from this tab menu. The new tab route invokes one target and does not batch or multiply work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited after the user selects the action; no provider call occurs while rebuilding tabs or opening the menu.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Provider work is constant per click. Local tab rebuild allocation grows linearly with visible tabs; the diff adds three lightweight actions per tab to an already full DOM/action rebuild.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One command per user activation; no burst across visible tabs. Tab rebuilds remain synchronous and only allocate/dispose local Action objects.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Capability and read-state observables are read directly; provider state is not prefetched. Per-tab actions are recreated with each rebuild and deterministically disposed by _tabDisposables.clear().
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the tab listener, command invocation, tab disposable lifecycle, and management/provider paths.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact provider latency varies, but cardinality is provably one and the menu path is explicit user interaction.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The new commands add constant, user-triggered work and the added action objects have bounded lifetime with explicit cleanup.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 25 changed files and all diff pages. Traced menu-opening UI work, dynamic action lifecycle, Date/group bulk read-state fan-out, provider IPC, serial bulk archive behavior, configuration persistence, and chat-tab command paths. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was introduced; no finding was submitted.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
